paras: The stoning of the Jas. Grimes house in Boone was a night attack in which a group of white men pelted the home of Jas. Grimes, a Black resident of Boone, North Carolina, with stones on a Thursday night in late January 1903, most likely 22 January. The stones broke many windows and frightened the occupants, and the house's owner offered a reward for the attackers' conviction. The town's weekly, the Watauga Democrat, condemned the attack in two items of its local column.

Grimes, described as "colored," lived in a "humble home" on the edge of Boone that belonged to a Mr. Coffey. The same column noted that some "colored people" in the village were destitute and sick with fever and urged white residents to help them.

According to the Watauga Democrat of 29 January, the attackers went to Grimes's home "on last Thursday night" and "proceeded to pelt it heavily with stones." The stones broke many panes of glass and frightened "the inmates almost into insensibility"; no injuries were reported. The paper did not name the attackers, identifying them only as "the white men" and, ironically, as "some gentlemen (?)."

Coffey offered a reward of $10 for the attackers' "apprehension and conviction." The editor wrote that "the arguseye of justice" was on their trail and that they would soon be caught, but no report of an arrest or prosecution was found.

The only known coverage is the Watauga Democrat, which ran two separate items on the same page of its local column. The first reported that "the general opinion of the people here" held the white men to be "far below" the "inoffensive negro" they had tried to humiliate. The second mocked the attackers as men "out of employment," called their conduct "almost unbearable" in a community "that boasts of civilization," and hoped for "the most rigid punishment."
No other white paper and no Black paper was found to have reported the attack.

quotes: The general opinion of the people here is that the white men who stoned the house of an inoffensive negro on last Thursday night are far below the ones they tried to humiliate by their ontlandish conduct.
On last Thursday night some gentlemen (?) being, we suppose, out of employment, went to the humble home of Jas. Grimes, colored, on the edge of town
